scope: Complete surviving1886 Brisbane Synagogue in its original six-vertex native whole-building envelope, including rear jog. Main high gabled nave and lower side aisles, pale rendered Moorish/Romanesque street facade, twin octagonal tower/arched belfry-like slots and pointed faceted metal spires/finials, central large circular geometric rose window in concentric arch, gable vent and friezes/coping, lower round entrance arch and own threshold/steps. Use original geometric tracery, no copied stained-glass artwork or religious lettering. Exclude surrounding Margaret Street/site, neighbor offices/sheds, fence/people/birds/wires, signs and interior.

references.caption:
Synagogue Church on Margaret Street, Brsibane, 1949
An allotment in Margaret Street was earmarked as the proposed site of the Brisbane Synagogue in 1885, with the foundation stone laid by Rev. A. P. Phillips on July 7th of that year. One year later, on the 18th of July 1886, the Brisbane Synagogue building was completed and consecrated with great ceremonies and celebrations. The building was designed by Arthur Morry, built by A. Midson, costing 5500 pounds. (Description supplied with photograph.).
